messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout rl-2026-03-17-42 — eu-west1 error rate spiked >5%. Automated rollback started but traffic still at ~12% on canary. Paging @eric (oncall). :rotating_light:
eric (oncall): on it, looking now. what auto-rollback steps ran?
maya (support): seeing 502s and tokenization errors hitting /v1/generate, spikes started ~23:18 UTC, customer tickets increasing. p50 +30% in EU.
jun (sre): auto rollback called `rlctl cancel` but session affinity kept some hosts routing to canary. sticky sessions + featureflag = partial drain failure.
amy (eng-runtime): that's the new-kv-cache flag. if it's on, some nodes keep warm KV state that isn't compatible with the rolled-back image. we should flip the flag kill-switch then force drain.
eric (oncall): understood. can we do a quick kill-switch then manual drain? want exact commands before touching prod.
amy (eng-runtime): yes — steps: 1) flip flag, 2) tell traffic controller to set canary=0, 3) scale down canary or evict pods. commands:```bash
# flip feature flag (our internal flag service)
flags-cli flip new-kv-cache --env=prod --value=false --note "emergency kill-switch for rl-2026-03-17-42"
# cancel rollout and set traffic
redwood rollout cancel rl-2026-03-17-42
redwood traffic set --target canary --percent 0 --env=prod
# scale down as a safety net
kubectl -n inference scale deploy model-serving-canary --replicas=0
```
jun (sre): I'll run the session-evict job after flag flip: `kubectl -n inference run evict-job --image=redwood/evict:stable -- /evict --label canary=true` — gives a clean sticky eviction.
liam (product): customer-facing note: CS streaming — we're seeing errors for EU customers on generation endpoints, flagged high priority. keep me posted on ETA to mitigate.
eric (oncall): proceeding with kill-switch. ping me when completed, then drain.
amy (eng-runtime): flipping now.
amy (eng-runtime): flags-cli: OK — new-kv-cache -> false :white_check_mark: (1715132476)
deploy-bot: flag change recorded: actor=amy (eng-runtime) note="emergency kill-switch" env=prod ts=1715132476
eric (oncall): invoking rollout cancel + traffic set now.
eric (oncall): `redwood rollout cancel rl-2026-03-17-42` -> OK
eric (oncall): `redwood traffic set --target canary --percent 0` -> in progress.
jun (sre): starting evict job now.
deploy-bot: traffic update: canary 8% -> 0% (gradual drain finished) ts=1715132504\jun (sre): evict job finished, pods with canary label drained and restarted onto stable pool.
amy (eng-runtime): scaling canary to 0 as extra safety.
amy (eng-runtime): `kubectl scale` -> OK.
eric (oncall): running quick smoke:```bash
curl -sS -I "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health" | head -n 1
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"smoke"}' | jq .status
```
eric (oncall): health 200, sample generate returned success, p95 trending back near baseline.
maya (support): CS: inbound tickets plateauing, no new critical reports in the last 5m. notifying customers in impacted region.\liam (product): noted — will coordinate postmortem comms.
eric (oncall): confirming error rate down <1% in eu-west1, latency back to normal. marking mitigation complete.
amy (eng-runtime): creating postmortem draft, linking logs and rollback timeline. tagging runtime and rollout teams.
jun (sre): I'll follow up on affinity cleanup and add a check in automated rollback to verify session drains.
eric (oncall): thanks all. handing to amy+jun for post-incident follow-up and root-cause. closing incident thread. :white_check_mark:
